title: Week Summary: Availability and Resilience Perspective

concepts.name: Availability
concepts.description: The degree to which a system is operational and usable when required.

concepts.name: Reliability
concepts.description: The degree to which a system performs correctly over time under stated conditions.

concepts.name: Resilience
concepts.description: The ability of a system to withstand, adapt to, and recover from disruptions.

concepts.name: Failure mode
concepts.description: A way in which a system, component, dependency, or process can fail.

concepts.name: Redundancy
concepts.description: The duplication of elements or capabilities to keep service available when one part fails.

concepts.name: Failover
concepts.description: The switch from a failed element to a backup element to continue service.

concepts.name: Graceful degradation
concepts.description: A mode where a system preserves critical functions while reducing nonessential capability during failure.

concepts.name: Recovery objective
concepts.description: A target such as recovery time or data loss tolerance that guides resilience design.

concepts.name: Observability
concepts.description: The ability to understand internal system state from outputs such as logs, metrics, traces, and events.

concepts.name: Incident review
concepts.description: A structured examination of an operational incident to learn causes, impacts, and improvement actions.

concepts.name: Resilience drill
concepts.description: A planned exercise that tests recovery processes, failure handling, and operational readiness.

concepts.name: Safe deployment
concepts.description: A release approach that limits blast radius and enables detection, rollback, or mitigation of problems.
